classification.reason: Customer is explicitly requesting a refund for the annual plan, which per policy must always be handled by a human manager.

draft.reply:
Hi,

Thanks for reaching out, and sorry to hear the annual plan hasn't been getting much use.

Our standard refund policy allows full refunds for requests made within 14 calendar days of the charge date. Since your annual plan was charged 20 days ago, this falls outside that standard window, so it isn't eligible for an automatic refund. Refund requests made after the 14-day window can still be approved as a goodwill exception, but that has to be reviewed and approved by a support manager — it's not something I'm able to approve directly.

I'm escalating your request to a manager on our team now, and they'll follow up with you directly to review it. Thanks for your patience in the meantime.

---
Sources for factual/policy claims:
- "Full refunds are available if requested within 14 calendar days of the charge date" — data/kb/refund_policy.md, item 1
- "Requests made after 14 calendar days are not eligible for a standard refund; may only be approved as a goodwill exception by a support manager, never by a first-line agent or automated system" — data/kb/refund_policy.md, item 2
- "For annual plans, the 14-day window applies to the annual charge date, not the original signup date" — data/kb/refund_policy.md, item 3
- "A support agent (human or automated) may confirm the policy... but must never promise a refund amount or approve a refund outright. Refunds are only executed by a manager." — data/kb/refund_policy.md, item 6

verification.notes: All citations are accurate and support their claims, the reply correctly declines to approve/promise a refund and escalates per policy, tone is professional, and the classifier's needs_human_approval=True is retained since nothing in the draft warrants overriding it.
